database_summary: This is a mixed analytical dataset (SQLite) containing weekly retail sales, cleaned sales, customer and shopping-cart event data, bitcoin members/transactions/prices, interest metrics and mapping, and several vegetable transaction/wholesale/category/loss tables. The schema mixes event streams (transactions, events), periodic measurements (weekly_sales, cleaned_weekly_sales, bitcoin_prices, interest_metrics), descriptive/dimensional tables (customer_regions, bitcoin_members, interest_map, shopping_cart_page_hierarchy, shopping_cart_event_identifier, shopping_cart_campaign_identifier, veg_cat, veg_loss_rate_df), and mapping/linking tables (customer_nodes, shopping_cart_users). Row counts indicate large event/measurement tables (veg_txn_df, bitcoin_transactions, shopping_cart_events). Use caution joining event tables to dimension tables as joins can multiply rows.

accepted.name: cleaned_weekly_sales_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date_formatted AS week_date_formatted,
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  transactions AS transactions,
  sales AS sales,
  week_number AS week_number,
  month_number AS month_number,
  calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  age_band AS age_band,
  demographic AS demographic,
  avg_transaction AS avg_transaction
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
accepted.description: Normalized/cleaned weekly sales rows with canonical date parts and preserved identifiers. Use this as the canonical cleaned weekly sales relation for time-series, aggregation, and joins. Parses week_date_formatted/week_date into ISO-like text where possible and exposes calendar_year, month_number, week_number and avg_transaction as-is. | Use for: time series of sales or transactions by region/platform/segment/customer_type; average transaction amount trends by demographic or age_band; year-over-year or month-over-month comparisons at weekly granularity

accepted.name: weekly_sales_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  transactions AS transactions,
  sales AS sales
FROM weekly_sales
accepted.description: Base pass-through view of weekly_sales preserving original columns. Use when the raw weekly_sales table is needed for comparisons or where cleaned_weekly_sales is not used. | Use for: raw weekly sales inspections; comparing raw and cleaned weekly sales; cohort selection by customer_type/segment/platform

accepted.name: bitcoin_transactions_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.txn_id AS txn_id,
  b.member_id AS member_id,
  m.first_name AS first_name,
  m.region AS region,
  b.ticker AS ticker,
  b.txn_date AS txn_date,
  b.txn_time AS txn_time,
  b.txn_type AS txn_type,
  b.quantity AS quantity,
  b.percentage_fee AS percentage_fee
FROM bitcoin_transactions b
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members m
  ON b.member_id = m.member_id
accepted.description: Bitcoin transactions enriched with member first_name and member region where available. Preserves txn-level grain and exposes transaction measures for downstream aggregation or member-level analysis. | Use for: member-level bitcoin activity; volume and fee summaries by member or region; time series of txn quantities for tickers or member segments

accepted.name: bitcoin_prices_daily
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS market_date,
  price AS price,
  open AS open,
  high AS high,
  low AS low,
  volume AS volume,
  change AS change
FROM bitcoin_prices
accepted.description: Canonical daily bitcoin prices relation (one row per ticker/market_date) preserving price, open/high/low and volume/change as provided. Use for price time-series and joins to transaction dates after parsing. | Use for: historical price lookups by ticker and date; join prices to transactions by date to compute P&L or price at txn date

accepted.name: shopping_cart_events_with_page
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id AS visit_id,
  e.cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  e.page_id AS page_id,
  p.page_name AS page_name,
  p.product_category AS product_category,
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  e.event_type AS event_type,
  e.sequence_number AS sequence_number,
  e.event_time AS event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
accepted.description: Enriched shopping cart events with page metadata (page_name, product_category, product_id). Preserves event-level grain and sequence_number for session reconstruction and funnel analysis. | Use for: session funnel and sequence analysis; page-level conversion and drop-off analysis; linking events to product categories for campaign analysis

accepted.name: shopping_cart_users_cookie_map
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id AS user_id,
  cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  start_date AS start_date
FROM shopping_cart_users
accepted.description: Mapping of shopping cart users to cookie_id and start_date. Use this to join cookie-based events to user identifiers and compute user cohorts by start_date. | Use for: attributing events/sessions to users; user cohort analysis from start_date; cross-system linking when cookie_id matches other member ids

accepted.name: interest_metrics_by_interest
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  interest_id AS interest_id,
  month_year AS month_year,
  _month AS _month,
  _year AS _year,
  composition AS composition,
  index_value AS index_value,
  ranking AS ranking,
  percentile_ranking AS percentile_ranking
FROM interest_metrics
accepted.description: Monthly interest metrics aggregated at interest_id/month_year grain, preserving index and composition measures along with ranking and percentile. Useful for time-series or ranking analyses of interests. | Use for: trend of index_value or composition for an interest; top-ranked interests by month/year using ranking or percentile_ranking

accepted.name: customer_transactions_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_type AS txn_type,
  txn_amount AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
accepted.description: Base customer transactions relation preserving customer_id, txn_date, txn_type, and txn_amount for downstream aggregations (LTV, recency, frequency). | Use for: customer spend summaries and aggregates; recency-frequency-monetary (RFM) calculations; filtering deposits vs withdrawals and their totals

accepted.name: veg_txn_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "index" AS "index",
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_time AS txn_time,
  item_code AS item_code,
  "qty_sold(kg)" AS "qty_sold(kg)",
  "unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS "unit_selling_px_rmb/kg",
  "sale/return" AS "sale/return",
  "discount(%)" AS "discount(%)",
  day_of_week AS day_of_week
FROM veg_txn_df
accepted.description: Base vegetable transactions at the transaction row level preserving item_code, txn_date/txn_time, quantity and unit price and other provided fields. Useful for sales, volume, and day-of-week analyses. | Use for: per-item sales volume and revenue; weekday vs weekend sales comparisons; impact of discounts on qty_sold

accepted.name: veg_item_master
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.item_code AS item_code,
  c.item_name AS item_name,
  c.category_code AS category_code,
  c.category_name AS category_name,
  l."loss_rate_%" AS "loss_rate_%"
FROM veg_cat c
LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df l
  ON c.item_code = l.item_code
accepted.description: Vegetable item master by joining category and loss-rate info to provide descriptive attributes for item_code. Preserves item_code as key and exposes item_name, category_name and loss_rate_%. | Use for: item-level margin or spoilage adjustments using loss_rate; category-level aggregations of sales or volume; labeling items with human-friendly names and categories

accepted.name: shopping_cart_events_ranked
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  visit_id AS visit_id,
  cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  page_id AS page_id,
  event_type AS event_type,
  sequence_number AS sequence_number,
  event_time AS event_time,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY visit_id ORDER BY sequence_number, event_time) AS row_rank
FROM shopping_cart_events
accepted.description: Event-level ranking within a visit ordered by sequence_number and event_time. Exposes a row_rank to allow downstream Top-K sequence filters (e.g., first N events per visit). | Use for: session-first-event or top-N event analyses; ordered funnel steps and transition timing

accepted.name: bitcoin_transactions_running_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  txn_id AS txn_id,
  member_id AS member_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_time AS txn_time,
  quantity AS quantity,
  SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY txn_time, txn_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_quantity
FROM bitcoin_transactions
accepted.description: Per-member running total of quantity over time (ordered by txn_time then txn_date) to support cumulative volume and staging for P&L/time-based queries. Preserves txn_id and member_id. | Use for: member cumulative volume and staging for retention cohorts; time-to-threshold analyses using running totals
